title: Seller's Guide to NYC Real Estate
subtitle: Maximize your property's value with strategic selling

sections.title: Preparing to Sell
sections.content:
Selling property in New York City requires strategic planning and expert guidance. This guide covers everything you need to know to achieve the best possible outcome.

**Key Considerations:**
- Current market conditions
- Your timeline and goals
- Property preparation and staging
- Pricing strategy

sections.title: Choosing the Right Time
sections.content:
### Market Timing
While you can't perfectly time the market, understanding trends helps. Spring typically sees the most activity, but quality properties sell year-round in NYC.

### Personal Timing
- Are you relocating for work?
- Do you need to coordinate with a purchase?
- What's your financial situation?

### Market Indicators
- Average days on market
- Inventory levels
- Price trends in your building/neighborhood
- Interest rate environment

sections.title: Pricing Your Property
sections.content:
### Comparative Market Analysis
Your agent will analyze recent sales of similar properties to determine fair market value.

**Factors Affecting Price:**
- Location and views
- Size and layout
- Building amenities
- Recent renovations
- Floor level and exposure
- Market conditions

### Pricing Strategy
- **Price it right from the start** - Overpriced listings stagnate
- **Consider micro-markets** - Your building and block matter
- **Account for co-op vs. condo differences** - Buyers factor in monthly costs

sections.title: Preparing Your Property
sections.content:
### Declutter and Depersonalize
Buyers need to envision themselves in the space. Remove excess furniture, personal photos, and collections.

### Repairs and Updates
- Fix obvious issues (leaky faucets, broken fixtures)
- Fresh paint in neutral colors
- Update dated fixtures if budget allows
- Deep clean everything

### Professional Staging
Staged homes often sell faster and for higher prices. Your agent can recommend professional stagers who know the NYC market.

sections.title: Marketing Your Property
sections.content:
### Professional Photography
High-quality photos are essential for online listings. Consider video tours and floor plans as well.

### Listing Distribution
- Multiple listing services (MLS)
- Major real estate portals
- Social media marketing
- Email to qualified buyers
- Broker networks

### Open Houses and Showings
Be flexible with showing times. Keep the property show-ready and make arrangements for pets during showings.

sections.title: The Selling Process
sections.content:
### 1. List Your Property
Sign listing agreement with your agent and launch marketing.

### 2. Show the Property
Accommodate buyer visits and open houses.

### 3. Receive and Negotiate Offers
Review all offers with your agent. Consider price, terms, buyer qualifications, and contingencies.

### 4. Accept an Offer
Sign the contract and collect deposit (typically 10%).

### 5. Buyer Due Diligence
Cooperate with inspections and board package preparation.

### 6. Board Approval (Co-ops)
Support buyer's application process.

### 7. Closing
Sign documents, transfer title, and receive proceeds.

sections.title: Costs of Selling
sections.content:
### Broker Commission
Typically 5-6% of sale price, split between listing and buyer's agents.

### Closing Costs
- Attorney fees ($2,000-4,000)
- Transfer taxes (NYC + NYS)
- Flip tax (many co-ops charge 1-3%)
- Mortgage payoff and satisfaction
- Move-out fees

### Tax Considerations
- Capital gains tax may apply
- Consult with a tax professional
- Consider 1031 exchange for investment properties
